name: Subject Control in a to-Infinitival Complement
pattern: Clause[Subject NPᵢ + V + to-infinitival with understood subjectᵢ]

entry.name: Subject Control in a to-Infinitival Complement
entry.pattern: Clause[Subject NPᵢ + V + to-infinitival with understood subjectᵢ]

1.definition: Interprets the matrix subject as undertaking, intending, or experiencing the subordinate situation.

relatedConstructions.notes: Jo promised to return assigns Jo a role in the promising. There seems to be a leak allows dummy there because the subject is selected through the infinitival.

projection.target: Jo is the promiser and the understood returner. A dummy there cannot replace Jo as the promiser.
projection.evidence: See the cited discussion and the constructed illustration.

curious.title: Who does the infinitive's action?
curious.summary: In some sentences, the person named at the start is also the one who does the action in the to-phrase.
curious.body: In Jo promised to return, Jo is the one who promises and also the one who returns. The to-phrase has no subject of its own, so we understand it as Jo. What matters is that Jo has a role in the promising: Jo takes on the undertaking, intention or experience described. A stand-in subject like the there of There seems to be a leak can't take over that role in the promising. This dictionary marks the analysis as provisional and bases it on one constructed illustration.

examples.text: There seems to be a leak.

curious.try: In Jo promised to return, who returns? Who promises? Is it the same person?

teacher.summary: Useful for explaining who performs the action in a to-infinitive after verbs like promise.
teacher.explain: The pattern is a clause whose subject is understood as the subject of the to-infinitival complement. The matrix subject undertakes, intends or experiences the subordinate situation: in Jo promised to return, Jo is both promiser and returner, so Jo is assigned a role in the promising. A dummy there cannot replace Jo as the promiser. That separates subject control from subject raising: in There seems to be a leak, dummy there is allowed because the subject is selected through the infinitival. This dictionary marks the analysis as provisional and rests on one constructed illustration.
teacher.terms: This dictionary’s term is subject control; the related pattern is subject raising. Textbooks sometimes describe the infinitival's missing subject as an understood subject.

contrasts.note: Jo has a role in the promising; control.

contrasts.text: There seems to be a leak.
contrasts.note: Dummy there is possible because the subject is selected through the infinitival; raising.

watch_for: A learner might think the to-phrase has no subject at all, when it is understood as the subject of the main verb.
A learner might treat promise and seem as the same pattern because both are followed by to.
teacher.activity: Students write sentences with verbs like promise, try and hope followed by a to-phrase. For each they say who does the second action and mark the link from the subject to the infinitive.

cite: Reynolds, Brett, ed. 2026. "Subject Control in a to-Infinitival Complement." English Constructionary. https://brettreynolds.ca/constructionary/linguist/subject-control-infinitival-001/ (snapshot 2026-11-19, ef810bb).
